justification: Design B pairs a serif body with a sans heading, numbers its sections, and keeps the Security callout beside the installation step it refers to (B2). Its code block and table sit within consistent margins (B3). Design A has a strong banner cover (A1), but its Security note is stranded at the top of page 2, away from the install step it belongs to. A's code block also overhangs the text margins (A1, A2), and its table is tighter. B's cover is plain but clean (B1). B reads as more orderly overall.

A has navy header and footer bands, numbered section headings, and a centred cover. Its tables are well proportioned with comfortable row spacing, and the final page keeps the Total row with the last accounts (A7). B has no bands and uses a left-aligned cover. Its heading and body indents are inconsistent, with headings at the margin and body text and tables indented (B2, B4). B leaves the Total row alone at the top of B7, orphaned from the table. B's wide table margins look slightly cramped.

A uses a geometric bold sans for headings, and its body indents stay consistent with the heading hierarchy. Procedures keep together: A4-A5 each fit whole, whereas B4 splits Procedure 4.3 so its step 1 sits on B4 and steps 2-4 on B5. B's heavy navy header and footer bands are repetitive, and its running header mismatches the page content ('2.1 Requirements' on the overview page). B's numbered headings are helpful and it makes denser use of pages, but A's title page is anchored better and its overall look is cleaner. A leaves a nearly empty page at A6, which is a minor weakness, and A's header text is slightly off too.

A has a dark green cover band with an orange accent rule and a consistent orange top band on interior pages. Its serif headings are elegant and its rules are tinted. B's cover is plain white with no band. Its sans headings hang outdented from the body text, which leaves the margins inconsistent. Its footers mix a running title with the page number. B does pack content more tightly, with no near-empty page, whereas A ends on a mostly empty page 5. A's overall polish and cover still make it the keeper.

A opens with a strong navy title band and carries running header and footer bands on later pages. It is compact at 4 pages, with consistent sans body and headings. Its flaws are the code block spilling past the left margin (A1), the callout stranded at the top of A2 away from the install step it refers to, and an empty lower half on A2. B's cover is mostly blank (B1), and its content is spread over 6 pages with sparse pages (B3, B6). B's headings and body are misaligned: the H2 sits at the far left while the body is indented, and the body is uneven in size (B4). B does keep the Security note beside the install step (B2), and its serif body is pleasant, but overall A reads as more polished and cohesive.

A pairs a bold sans heading with a serif body, giving a clearer hierarchy. Its section numbers (1.1, 2.1) match the table of contents, and the navy running header and footer give a consistent frame (A2, A3, A4). The divider pages show a large numeral beside the title (A5, A8). The big '148m' stat is strong in both designs. B is elegant, but its light serif headings feel weaker and its gold top rule with logo adds little. B's divider pages lack the numeral, and its table and charts are comparable to A's but slightly lighter (B5, B6). A's page furniture also helps navigation.

B adds a table of contents (B2) and numbered section headings (B3, B5, B7), which make it easier to navigate. Its sans headings over serif body text read well, and its chart axes have fuller ticks (B4, B6). A has a consistent sans face, but it has no contents page and its section openers carry no numerals (A4). Its Who rides heading on A6 is light and weaker than the other headings. Both designs leave large empty areas on the data pages, and A's charts have sparser axes (A3, A5).

A has a navy header and footer band on every interior page showing the running title and section name, plus numbered section headings and a bold sans heading that stands out against the serif body. These make it easy to navigate (A2, A4). The tables are legible, with a tinted FY2026 column and a clear total row (A7). B has a darker full-bleed cover that looks striking (B1) and an elegant serif, but its running footer is faint and the top rule is thin. Its balance-sheet table splits after only two rows (B4), which leaves an orphaned fragment. A's split is less awkward, since five rows stay together before the break (A4).

B has a strong colored cover band with the title and content starting on page 1, plus running header and footer bands that give structure. Its content flows continuously with few large gaps. A spends a full page on a sparse cover and leaves page 6 mostly empty. A's heading indents are also inconsistent: H1 sits further left than the body text. A does keep the security callout together with the install block, while B splits it onto the next page, and B splits Procedure 3 across pages. Overall B is more cohesive.

A uses a refined serif (EB Garamond-like) with a thin gold rule and a small logo mark, which looks elegant and consistent. B adds heavy navy header and footer bars, and its sans/serif mix feels busier. B's numbered headings and running section titles aid navigation, and its section dividers (B5, B9) have bigger numerals, but the section number 3 is missing from its divider set and the 'Who rides' heading on B7 is light compared with the others. A's dividers are cleaner (A5, A9), though A's 'Who rides' heading on A7 is also unstyled.

B is more compact and better filled. Its cover is merged with the overview on page 1, and the banner, running headers and footer bands are consistent. A spends a full page on a sparse cover, and its pages 3 and 6 are mostly empty. A's Security callout stays beside the install command it relates to, which is a plus, but B splits the callout from its code block across pages 1 and 2. B also splits Procedure 3's list across pages 3 and 4, which hurts rhythm. A's serif body with bold headings reads well, but its Troubleshooting page is nearly empty. Tables look similar in both designs; B's is slightly crisper. Overall B is tighter and more coherent despite the awkward page breaks.

Design B has a dark full-bleed cover, a refined serif, a quiet top rule and a clean footer. Its sections start on new pages, which gives a steady rhythm, and Troubleshooting gets its own page. Design A has numbered headings and a running header, which help navigation (A2, A5). But its heavy dark header and footer bars look cramped, its steps split across pages (A4 to A5), and its cover is small, floating and unbalanced (A1). B's drawbacks are an almost empty last page (B6) and slightly lighter heading hierarchy.

B has a full-bleed illustrated cover (B1) and a consistent gold-rule system with a running header. Its content flows continuously across B2-B4 with no big empty gaps, and its serif text, green accents and shaded 2025 columns look cohesive. A has a green band cover, but A1 leaves the lower half of the page blank. A's headings hang left of indented body text, which looks awkward. A3's full-bleed image is cropped oddly against the page edge. A's tables and charts are fine and comparable to B's. B's cover title sits over the building windows, which hurts legibility slightly.

A has a table of contents (A2), numbered section headings and a large numeral on the divider pages (A5, A8), with a serif body face that pairs well with the sans headings. Its charts carry more axis ticks and numbered subsection titles (A4, A6). A's last page, with the Costs and carbon content, is not shown, so only 8 of its 9 pages can be compared. B is consistent and clean but has no contents page and a single sans family throughout, and its dividers are less distinctive (B4, B7). In both designs the pages are mostly empty below the content, so whitespace is a wash.

A has a real table of contents (A2) and a serif/sans pairing. Its section headings flow into the content on A4-A6, so pages are fuller and the pacing is steadier. A's charts are monochrome with a highlighted final year, and their axes are legible. B's page 'Who rides' heading is weak, set in light weight (B6). B uses nearly empty divider pages (B4, B7) and leaves large empty areas under short content on B3, B5, B6 and B8, which breaks the rhythm. B's header and footer bands and sidebar navigation are tidy and consistent but add weight and waste pages. B's tables and charts are clean and its blue palette is cohesive.

B is compact: a teal title band on the cover page and three full pages, with orange rules separating sections, so it keeps a steady rhythm. A spends a mostly empty cover page and leaves large blank areas on A2, A3 and A5, and its tables split awkwardly (the parameters table is separated from section 3, A3 to A4). A's bold numbered headings are stronger than B's light, small headings, which look weak against the body text, and B's appendix heading is tiny. Overall B's balance and flow win.

B has a full-bleed cover (B1) with a serif title over the illustration, and a pull-quote that gives the report a more editorial, finished feel. Its running header and footer are quieter. A packs the title into a green band on page 1 (A1) and the same illustration is cropped on A2. B's body text is looser and breathes more, while A has justified text with hyphenation (A2) and tighter spacing. B's page 4 chart has a fuller axis and a clearer rhythm. A's coloured bands and Barlow type are crisp, and its stat row is well grouped, but B reads as the more polished and keepable document.

A has a full-bleed cover with a skyline illustration and a green band, plus consistent running headers and numbered headings. Its green accent colour is used across the stat blocks, chart and tables. Pages 2-4 are well filled, and the photo is sized sensibly within the margins. B's cover is only a green header band, and its first page leaves the bottom half empty. B's headings sit outdented from the body text, which looks misaligned. B's image is full-bleed and oversized, running off the right edge of the page. Its grey charts look flat and its pull quote is oversized.

A packs the content into 3 pages with a strong teal title band on the cover (A1) and orange rules separating sections. Pages are well filled and the tables stay with their sections (A2, A3). B spends a whole page on a sparse centered title (B1) and leaves large empty areas on B2, B3 and B5. B also splits the configuration table from its section onto the next page (B4). B's numbered headings and serif body are clean, but the page flow is weaker.

A has a dark full-bleed cover with a strong title and consistent margins. Its section headings and table headers are aligned to the content column. B's section headings sit outdented from the body and tables, and its tables run wider than the text column, so the alignment looks inconsistent. B's last page holds only a stranded Total row, which leaves an orphaned table fragment. A's last page keeps eight account rows together with the Total and Notes. A's repeated heavy top rule gives a steady running rhythm across pages.

A keeps the config parameters table on page 3 with its firmware text and fits the content into 4 pages. Its heading rules create clear section breaks, and the left-aligned cover is confident. B splits the config table away from its section onto page 4, leaves page 5 almost empty with one small table, and its heavy header and footer bands crowd the page. B's numbered headings and centered cover are tidy, but A's indent of headings against body text is slightly odd.

A uses an elegant serif with gold rules and a large pull quote, so sections read cleanly and the cover title sits over a layered skyline. B's justified text produces hyphenation breaks (de-livered, suppli-ers, assur-ance) and uneven word spacing, and its cover splits into a crude image block over a flat green band. B's numbered bold sans headings and running headers are tidy but generic, and its small italic quote is weak. The tables and charts are comparable in both. A's page 3 image is full width and more integrated.

Design B is the more cohesive, finished report. Its cover pairs the illustration with a green band (B1). Running headers and footers, numbered sections and green-tinted charts and tables give it a consistent accent colour (B2-B4). A's grey charts and tables clash with its green header band. A's first page is half empty, and its full-bleed illustration is cropped awkwardly (A1, A3). A's one-section-per-page layout also leaves large empty areas (A2, A4). A's large pull quote is a strong touch, but B's denser flow is more balanced overall.

B adds navy header and footer bands with running titles and 'Page x of 7', numbered section headings and a cover centred on the page, so it reads as a finished report. Its tables carry on across pages with repeated headers and the Total row sits with the last data rows (B7). A is cleaner, with a bold heading font and a left-aligned cover, but it strands the lone Total row on A7 and has no bands. A's page 4 balance sheet start is better than B's, which leaves only five rows before a break (B4). Overall B is more polished and consistent.

B reads as a more polished manual: a full-bleed cover, a serif body with clear headings, and consistent page margins. Its security note stays attached to the install step (B2), and the procedure pages break cleanly (B4, B5). A packs a header band and the title into page 1 with no cover, and it splits the security callout from the install code onto A2. Its procedure list also breaks mid-list across A3 and A4. A's code block on A1 overhangs the text margins. B has a sparse final page (B6) and a mostly empty cover, but A also leaves large gaps (A2). The tables are similar, with B's slightly more refined. A's running header bands are a plus for navigation.

A has numbered headings, a centered cover and teal header and footer bands that give clear navigation (A2). Its tables sit on consistent margins, but pages A3 to A5 end with large empty areas and A5 holds a single small table. B's headings hang left of an indented body, which looks misaligned (B2). B's rules above each heading add clutter, and the Appendix heading is demoted, though its denser four pages use space better. B's tables and image are fine, but its overall structure is less polished.

A has a dark full-bleed cover with a left-aligned serif title, and a light serif body with airy tables and a restrained footer. B's cover is plain, centered and sparse. B also adds heavy navy header and footer bands on every page, which feel boxy, and its justified intro text gives uneven word spacing. B's table rows are denser and its table splits are less tidy. B does number its sections and repeats the section name in the header, which helps navigation, but A's overall polish and calmer rhythm make it the one a careful reader would keep.

A uses bold sans headings that clearly outrank the body text. B's section headings (Overview, Installation, Configuration) are light-weight serif, barely heavier than the body, so the hierarchy is weaker (B2, B3). A's headings are also better separated from the rules above them. A's running footer shows the current section, which is more useful than B's repeated title. B's dark cover band and top rule on every page are more striking, but the cover title is small and the top rule adds clutter. A's margins are inconsistent, since H1 headings sit outdented from the body, but this is minor. Tables, code blocks and the diagram are near-identical in both designs.

B pairs a serif with sans chart labels and gives a more bookish, refined look. It adds a table of contents, a gold top rule and a logo. Its charts use fuller y-axes, and its table has more generous row spacing (B6, B3). A has strong header and footer bands and a consistent sans-serif, but its small header and footer text is cramped. Its page 6 heading 'Who rides' is lighter than the other headings, and its charts have sparse axes (A3, A6). Both designs leave large empty areas on the content pages. Overall B feels slightly more polished.

A opens with a navy title band and puts running header and footer bands on the inner pages. It starts each section (Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Notes) on a clean page, so the sections stay distinct. Its sans-serif table type is crisp, and the shaded FY2026 column and total row help scanning. B has a mostly empty dark cover and a serif face, which reads less clearly in dense numeric tables. B also breaks the Balance Sheet awkwardly, leaving only two rows under the heading at the bottom of page 4. The footers on B are tiny and the top rule is the only banding.

A has a full cover page with illustration and clear bold numbered headings (A2, A4) over serif body text, which gives strong hierarchy. Its charts are larger and carry fuller axes, and the image is framed with a caption (A3). B's headings are light and weak, so the hierarchy is flatter. Its cropped, full-width image looks clumsy (B2). Its section pages leave large empty areas at the bottom (B2, B3). B's green header band and gold rules are a nice touch but do not outweigh these problems.

B puts the title on a navy band at the top of its first page and carries navy header and footer bands on every page, so it feels cohesive. Its tables are denser and tidier, with a bold total row that stays attached to its table on B6. A spends a full page on a mostly empty cover and leaves the total row orphaned at the top of A7. The A income statement also breaks after the Q3 Cost of sales row, which looks arbitrary. A's serif body text is pleasant, but its page layout is less consistent. B's headings are light in weight, which is a small weakness.

B puts the title in a navy band and the income statement on the same page, so the content starts at once. Its running header and footer bands, with section names and 'Page x of 6', help a reader navigate. Its sans-serif tables are dense but clear, and each page is filled evenly, with the balance sheet starting on a fresh page (B4). A has an elegant serif and more generous whitespace, but its cover is a mostly empty dark page (A1) and its thin footer is weak. The balance sheet starts at the bottom of A4 with only two rows, then splits across pages. A7 is left mostly empty. A's row spacing is looser and its pages are less consistently filled.

A's bold numbered sans headings make the section structure clear on A2-A4, and its green cover band keeps the title legible (A1). B's headings are light and weak, and its repeated gold rules and logo add clutter (B2-B4). B's cover title sits over the building windows and is hard to read (B1). B's pull quote is large and decorative, but the page lacks hierarchy overall. The tables are similar in both. A's justified text sometimes hyphenates awkwardly.

A opens with a strong navy title band and carries navy header and footer bands on every page. Its section titles are clear, and the balance sheet starts on its own page (A4). Its tables are comfortably spaced, and the total row and Notes sit together on the last page (A6). B has a mostly empty cover (B1) and a balance sheet that starts mid-page after the income table (B4). B's last page holds only a Total row orphaned from its table, plus a short note (B7). B's table text is smaller and its serif body font is less crisp. B's layout is clean but weaker overall.

A is compact, three pages, with a strong teal title band, running header and footer bands, and tables kept with their text (A2, A3). B has a mostly empty cover, then pages with large blank areas (B2, B3, B5), the configuration table split from its section onto the next page (B4), and a nearly empty last page. B's serif type is elegant, but its flow and page balance are weaker.

A has a strong dark-green cover with left-aligned serif title and orange accent. Its section rules and generous spacing give a calm, editorial rhythm, and its footer is light. B uses heavy teal header and footer bands on every page that add clutter, and a plain centred cover. B's bold numbered sans headings are clear but denser, with tighter spacing between sections. The content is otherwise identical.

A has a full-bleed illustrated cover (A1) and a consistent gold-accent palette. Its pages are continuous, with a running header and footer, and its serif headings sit on the same margin as the body text (A2-A4). B has a plain cover band, and its page 1 is half empty (B1). B's headings hang outside the indented body, so the left alignment is ragged. B also has hyphenation and justification gaps and a full-bleed image that overshoots the margins (B3). The tables are comparable, but A's palette is more cohesive.

B numbers its headings, so the hierarchy is clearer. Its running header and footer help navigation, and the content flows more continuously. The troubleshooting section sits on page 5 instead of leaving page 6 nearly empty as A does. A's dark cover is bold, but it is bottom-heavy and plain beyond the title. A also has a sparse last page and an uneven page 5. B's table header is stronger. B splits Procedure 3 across pages 4 and 5, which is a minor flaw.

B has a consistent system: running header and footer bands, numbered sections, and divider pages with a side tab that shows where the reader is. Its blue charts and table match the palette, and one accent colour ties the pages together (B2, B4, B5, B6). A packs sections onto shared pages with no page-level framing. Section headings in A sit oddly left of the text margin (A4, A5, A6), and A5 is cramped. B has some sparse pages, such as B7 and B9, but its rhythm is steadier. A's greyscale charts are clean but dull.

A has numbered headings, navy header and footer bands with running titles and page counts, and a centered cover. It fits into 5 pages with consistent flow (A2, A4, A5). B has an inconsistent left indent where headings sit outside the body, so the margins look uneven (B2, B3). It also has a sparse, nearly empty last page (B6), and the cover is left-aligned and low. B's body text size varies between 'Confirm' lines on B4. B's tables and code blocks are similar to A's. A's code block has a minor flaw: the header strip overhangs (A3).

A pairs a serif body with clear section headings and a full-bleed cover with an orange accent rule, so it reads as a manual a person would keep (A1, A2). Its tables are clean, but pages 4 and 5 leave a lot of empty space. B packs content more densely under a sans-serif face. Its headings are light and weak, with the appendix heading no stronger than body text (B3). Its header and footer bands are heavy but consistent. B's cover is only a banner on the first page, and its title and body text are less refined.

B packs content into three pages with consistent green and gold accents, a running header band, and tinted charts that match the palette. A leaves page 1 more than a third empty and splits each section onto its own page with large blank areas. A's image bleeds off the right edge and its text is indented unevenly against the headings. B's chart and table are split across pages 1-2, which is a minor flaw.

A pairs a refined serif with a dedicated cover (A1), and the pull quote on A2 is large and distinct, which makes the hierarchy more editorial. Its body text is left-aligned, so it avoids the justified rivers and hyphenation breaks in B ("re-placement", B2). B's cover band is clean and the running header is useful, but its sans type is plainer, the quote is small, and the three pages carry a lot of empty space at the bottom. The tables are similar in both, and A's pages show a steadier rhythm.

A uses bold sans headings with numbered sections and a running header and footer band, so the section structure is clear (A2, A4). B's headings are light serif, barely larger than body text, and the Appendix heading is styled differently from the others (B5). B's dark cover is stronger than A's plain centered cover (B1 vs A1), and its orange rules are a nice touch. Overall A's hierarchy and navigation win.

A is more compact and cohesive. Its green cover band, gold rules and green accents hold together across A1-A3, with running headers and consistent margins. The chart sits on the same page as the climate text (A1) and the pull quote is subtle. B spends page 1 mostly empty below the quote. Its left-hanging headings are misaligned with the indented body text. The image on B3 bleeds off the right edge, which looks unbalanced. B's grey charts and tables are muted and less distinctive. A does have blank space at the bottom of pages 2 and 3, and its image is cropped, but overall it reads as more polished.

Scores follow the scale where positive favours A and negative favours B. B opens with a strong title band, so the cover and first content share page 1 and the document has no wasted page. B's sans body text is clean and its table is clear. B does split the Security callout from its code block onto the next page (B2), and the code block slightly overhangs the margins. A spends a full page on a sparse cover (A1). Its numbered headings (1 Overview, 2.1 Requirements) give clearer structure, and its running header section labels are helpful. A also keeps the callout attached to the install steps (A2). But A's pages have large empty gaps (A3), and its serif body is a little less crisp. B is somewhat more compact and cohesive overall.

A uses a refined serif with a navy and gold palette, which looks editorial and well kept (A1, A3). It also adds a table of contents (A2). Its table has clean rules and generous row spacing (A6). B's sans-serif is competent but plainer. B's heavy header and footer bands crowd the pages, and the "Who rides" heading is light next to its subhead (B6). A's section dividers and B's are nearly identical. Both leave large empty areas on the content pages. A has a slight edge overall.

A opens with a strong teal title band and puts content on the first page, with running header and footer bands that aid navigation. Its headings are consistent, and the orange rules and teal-ruled tables feel cohesive. B spends a mostly empty page on the cover. Its headings hang in the left margin with indented body text, which looks slightly awkward. Its serif body reads fine, and its tables are clean but plainer. The appendix heading in B is bold while the same heading in A is light, so B is more consistent there, but A is better overall.

A uses bold sans headings with body text indented under them, so sections are easy to find (A2, A4). Its tables stay beside the text that introduces them, and the content fits in 4 pages. B has light, low-contrast headings, an orange rule and top band on every page, and the config table is split from its section onto a separate page. B's last page is almost empty (B5). B's dark cover is bolder than A's plain white one, but that does not outweigh these issues.

A gives each section a clear divider with a sidebar band that marks progress, and has a running header with a gold rule. Its navy and gold palette is consistent, and the serif headings are refined. The chart pages (A4, A6, A7) are clean, though several pages are left mostly empty. B packs sections together: the Reliability heading sits mid-page on B4, and its section rules extend into the left margin, so the headings look misaligned with the text. B's justified body text is spaced unevenly. B's dense layout does avoid the empty space, but it feels less polished and has no bands. A's page numbers also match its table of contents, while B's TOC entries look off (Reliability is listed on page 4 and the efficiency charts are on 6).

B has a dark full-bleed cover (B1) and a consistent top band on each page. Its tables carry the total row with the data on B7, and the Notes sit beneath it. A's cover is plain, and its total row is orphaned onto A7 alone, with Notes after it on a mostly empty page. A's bold sans headings are strong, but its tables break awkwardly, leaving an orphaned total and a heading separated from its table by a page break. B also splits the Balance Sheet table after two rows (B4), which is a flaw, though a smaller one. B's serif type is elegant and its tables are consistently set.

B has a strong teal title band on the first page, with the content starting right away, so the opening page is purposeful. Its running header and footer bands give consistent navigation. A's cover page is mostly empty and takes a whole page. A has bolder headings, but its headings sit outdented from the indented body text, which looks slightly awkward. The tables and image are similar in both. B's thin heading weight is a minor weakness, but its overall structure is more cohesive.

B fills the cover with a navy band and puts the income statement on the same page, so it is more compact and has a stronger cover (B1). A's cover is a nearly empty page with a small title (A1). A's tables have more generous row spacing and numbered section headings, and its balance sheet starts on a page with the tail of the income table, which is a bit awkward (A4). Both use the same table styling and a blue shaded column, so the tables are close. B's lighter condensed type is slightly thinner but still clear. A's roomier rows and clearer section numbering make it slightly easier to read, but B's strong cover and tighter pagination are the more polished.

A opens with a compact green title band over the commitments, so page 1 carries real content, and gold rules mark each section consistently (A1). Its section headings are light, and the clear running header band suits the report (A2, A3). B spends its first page on a cover whose image is cropped at the right edge and whose title block is plain (B1). B's bold numbered headings are clear and its tables are good, but the page 3 image has an awkward dark base and the layout is more generic (B3). A's photo is cropped at the bottom (A2), a flaw similar to B's. A's justified text has some wide gaps, though B has hyphenation too.

A spends eight pages on thin content: pages A2, A3, A5, A6 and A8 are mostly empty below short content, and the divider pages A4 and A7 add little. Its sidebar dividers and header and footer bands are distinctive and consistent, but the blank space looks wasteful. B flows sections continuously with a TOC (B2), so pages are fuller and rhythm is steadier (B4, B5, B6). The serif body with sans headings reads well, and the table on B5 is clean with a heavy rule. B's section headings sit slightly left of the body indent and the justified text has loose spacing, which are minor flaws. B's monochrome charts are less colourful than A's blue ones, but they stay legible.

A gives each section a divider page with a sidebar tab, uses running header and footer bands, and keeps a consistent blue accent in charts and table, so it reads as a polished report. It leaves many pages largely empty (A3, A4, A7), which costs balance and whitespace. B flows content continuously and is compact, but its section headings (Reliability, Who rides) hang out into the left margin with full-width rules, and they begin mid-page. B's grey and black charts are plain, and its page footers are weak (B4, B5).

A opens with a strong navy title band and puts the income statement on the first page. Its sans-serif tables are consistent, and the balance sheet starts on a fresh page with a clean header (A4). B spends page 1 on a sparse cover with a small title (B1). It also strands a balance sheet heading with only five rows at the bottom of B4, and the serif figures feel less crisp. B's numbered section headings are a plus, but they don't outweigh these issues.

A has a dark navy cover band, a top rule on content pages, and consistent left alignment of headings, body, code and table (A2, A3). B's headings hang out to the left of the indented body text, the content block sits off-center, and the heavy sans headings clash with the serif body (B2, B3). B's running footer, which repeats section names, is slightly useful but looks noisy. Both share the clipped 'Worker' label in the diagram and the empty placeholder dashboard.

B gives each chapter its own divider page with a side navigation band, and it adds a running header and accent rule. Its serif type is consistent, and its charts and table sit cleanly on their own pages (B4, B5, B7).
